rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening recalls the selection of Imran’s family and explains how that selection occurred.
rows.anchor: تقرير للاصطفاء وبيان لكيفية والظرف فى حيز النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause is the object of an omitted command, meaning ‘remember the time when she said.’
rows.anchor: أى اذكر لهم وقت قولها وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construes the time phrase with the preceding ‘All-Hearing, All-Knowing’ by syntactic competition.
rows.anchor: هو منصوب على الظرفية لما قبله وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis attaches the time phrase to the implied meaning of ‘He selected,’ joining clause to clause rather than constituent to constituent.
rows.anchor: ظرف لمعنى الاصطفاء المدلول عليه باصطفى المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran’s wife is Hanna daughter of Faqūdhā, identified in reports from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra; she is Jesus’ maternal grandmother.
rows.anchor: كما رواه إسحق ابن بشر عن ابن عاس رضى الله تعالى عنه والحاكم عن أبى هريرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Alusi cites Ishaq ibn Bishr from Ibn Abbas and al-Hakim from Abu Hurayra for Hanna’s identity.
rows.anchor: كما رواه إسحق ابن بشر عن ابن عاس رضى الله تعالى عنه والحاكم عن أبى هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historians say Hanna’s sister Isha married Zakariya and became Yahya’s mother, making Jesus and Yahya maternal cousins.
rows.anchor: وكان لها أخت اسمها إيشاع تزوجها زكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام هى أم يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Miʿraj report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections calls Jesus and Yahya sons of a maternal aunt, which appears to conflict with the cousin relationship.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه الشيخان فى حديث المعراج من قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: صاحب التقريب
rows.claim: The al-Taqrib author explains the Miʿraj wording figuratively: men sometimes call a female cousin ‘aunt’ affectionately, indicating maternal kinship.
rows.anchor: وأجاب صاحب التقريب بأن الحديث مخرج على المجاز فإنه كثيرا ما يطلق الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A competing genealogy makes Isha Hanna’s maternal half-sister and Maryam’s paternal sister, by proposing Imran first married Hanna’s mother and later Hanna.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت إيشاع أخت حنة من الام وأخت مريم من الاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds that genealogy weak: it conflicts with the account that Isha and Hanna were both daughters of Faqūdhā and lacks reports for either marriage claim.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه مخالف لما ذكره يحيى السنة من أن إيشاع وحنة بنتا فاقوذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits from Ibn Abbas that childless, amenorrheic Hanna saw a bird feed its chick, longed for a child, prayed for a son, and menstruated immediately.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن حنة امرأة عمران كانت حبست عن الولد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the same report Hanna vowed the child to sacred service once she believed she was pregnant; only boys were then dedicated, and her husband warned that a girl would not be accepted.
rows.anchor: لئن نجانى الله تعالى ووضعت ما فى بطنى لأجعله محررا ولم يكن يحرر فى ذلك الزمان إلا الغلمان

words: رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a girl would not qualify for the dedication, Hanna’s vow also implicitly asks God to make the child male, like asking that a servant be freed on one’s behalf.
rows.anchor: وهذا فى الحقيقة استدعاء للولد الذكر لعدم قبول الانثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some imams take the wording as emphasizing her vow and changing its conditional form into a direct declaration.
rows.anchor: وجعله بعض الائمة تأكيدا لنذرها وإخراجا له عن صورة التعليق إلى هيئة التنجيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of ‘for You’ expresses purpose: the child is dedicated to serving God’s sanctuary.
rows.anchor: واللام من ( لك ) للتعليل ولمراد لخدمة بيتك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains muḥarraran as one devoted to temple service, abstaining from worldly affairs and marriage for worship and service of the church.
rows.anchor: والمحرر من يعمل للدنيا ولا يتزوج ويتفرغ لعمل الآخرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses muḥarraran as a servant of the church.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : المحرر الخادم للبيعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A second report from Mujahid defines the word as pure, with nothing of worldly life mixed into the person.
rows.anchor: وفى رواية عنه الخالص الذى لا يخالطه شئ من أمر الدنيا

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says Hanna meant a person freed and wholly devoted to obedience, not used for her own needs.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير : أرادت عتيقا خالصا لطاعتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term derives from freedom in two senses: exemption from enslavement and freedom from base traits and worldly vices.
rows.anchor: وعلى كل هو من الحرية وهى ضربان أن لا يجرى عليه حكم السبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran is most properly a circumstantial accusative describing mā, governed by ‘I vowed’; the state may be prospective or accompanying.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه على الحالية من ( ما ) والعامل فيه ( نذرت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes it a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in ‘for You,’ governed by an implied predicate of existence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من الضمير الذى فى الجار والمجرور والعامل فيه حينئذ الاستقرار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan permits reading the form as an accusative verbal noun, taḥrīran, because it conveys the sense of the vow.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان أن ينصب على المصدر أى تحريرا لانه بمعنى النذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording signals the abundance of Hanna’s desire for what she is asking.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة للايذان بوفور الرغبة فى مضمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the prepositional phrase first marks her particular concern for God.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الجار والمجرور لكمال الاعتناء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child is called mā to leave its identity and sex indefinite and because it has not reached the rank of rational beings.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن الولد بما لإبهام أمره وفصوره عن درجة العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqabbul is to receive something approvingly; its root sense is meeting or requiting with recompense, while here it means to accept.
rows.anchor: و التقبل أخذ الشئ على وجه الرضا وأصله المقابلة بالجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears every audible thing and knows what has been and will be, including Hanna’s intention.
rows.anchor: لسائر المسموعات فتسمع دعائى العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of the sincerity of her intention explains her request for acceptance as a plea for gracious favor.
rows.anchor: وهو تعليل لاستدعاء القبول من حيث ان علمه تعالى بصحة نيتها وإخلاصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic clause displays her firm certainty in what she states.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة أغرض قوة يقينها بمضمونها

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Restricting hearing and knowledge to God focuses the prayer on Him and cuts off all hope in anything else.
rows.anchor: قاله شيخ الإسلام وتقديم صفة السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is mentioned before knowledge because hearing’s innumerable objects are fewer than knowledge’s.
rows.anchor: وتقديم صفة السمع لان متعلقاتها وإن كانت غر متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Maryam as the vowed offering in place of the expected boy, likening the vow to a gift and divine approval to receiving it.
rows.anchor: أى رضى بمريم فى النذر مكان الذكر ففيه تشبيه النذر بالهدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun most properly refers to Maryam’s Lord, who brought her to the perfection fitting her.
rows.anchor: رب مريم المبلغ لها إلى كما لها اللائق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as Hanna, since she was the one who spoke and called, ‘My Lord, I have delivered her.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لامرأة عمران بدليل أنها التى خاطبت ونادت بقولها ( رب إني وضعتها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabūl can denote the means by which something is accepted, just as suʿūṭ and ladūd name what is used for nasal or oral administration.
rows.anchor: و القبول ما يقبل به الشئ كالسعوط واللدود ما يسعط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good acceptance means God uniquely honored her to stand in for a male dedication, or received her from her mother at birth before she was ready for service.
rows.anchor: تقبلها بوجه حسن تقبل به النذائر وهو اختصاصه سبحانه إياها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Hanna, fearing a girl could not be consecrated, placed Maryam by the Jerusalem priests; after successive lots with writing pens and pens thrown in the Jordan, Zakariya’s pen prevailed and he took her.
rows.anchor: فقد روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : لما وضعتها خشيت حنة أن لا تقبل الأنثى محرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may indicate association, with qabūl a verbal noun and an omitted complement: she was accepted in a state worthy of approval.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الباء للملابسة و القبول مصدر وهو من المصادر الشاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafaʿʿala may function like istafʿala here, so the phrase means God received and welcomed her from her first moment of life.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تفعل بمعنى استفعل كتعجل بمعنى استعجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading God showed a special karāma in Maryam from birth.
rows.anchor: وأظهر الكرامة فيها حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis treats the bāʾ as extra and qabūlan as an emphatic verbal noun, with the unusual form conveying complete approval and solicitude.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الباء زائدة و القبول مصدر مؤكد للفعل السابق بحذف الزوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tafaʿʿala ordinarily suggests effort against the agent’s nature; for God it conveys the resulting power and abundance of the act.
rows.anchor: فان صيغة التفعل مشعرة بحسب أصل الوضع بالتكلف وكون الفعل على خلاف طبع الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A remote reading makes the bāʾ mean ‘with’: God accepted the vow alongside Hanna’s prayer for Maryam and her descendants to be protected from Satan throughout life.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل على بعد بعيد أن تكون الباء للمصاحبة بمعنى مع أى تقبل نذرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the good growth as raising Maryam in worship and obedience to her Lord.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما وفي رواية عنه أنه سوى خلقها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Maryam’s form was made proportionate and she grew in one day as much as others grow in a year.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عنه أنه سوى خلقها فكانت تشب في يوم ما يشب غيرها في عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God cared for her in every circumstance, figuratively like a gardener watering, protecting, and clearing weeds from a crop.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تعهدها بما يصلحها في سائر أحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The care image is either a representational metaphor or a metonymy based on necessary association with tending a crop.
rows.anchor: فقي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية أو مجاز مرسل بعلاقة اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabatan is a verbal noun unlike the verb’s form and substitutes for inbāt.
rows.anchor: و ( نباتا ) هنا مصدر على غير لفظ الفعل المذكور وهو نائب عن إنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the implied wording is ‘she grew with good growth’; nabāt and nabt are synonymous and may also refer to the plant itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : التقدير فنبتت نباتا والنبات والنبت بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya was descended from Solomon son of David.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكر فى حديث ابن عباس وكل ذلك من آثار قدرته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought Maryam to Zakariya and made him her guardian and guarantor of her interests, as in the Ibn Abbas report; this was divine power, not revelation to Zakariya.
rows.anchor: أى ضمها الله تعالى إليه وجعله كافلا لها وضامنا لمصالحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and ʿAsim (except Ibn ʿAyyash’s transmission) geminate the fāʾ and shorten Zakariyyā, making him the object of ‘entrusted.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ بتشديد الفاء حمزة والكسائي وعاصم وقصروا ( زكريا ) غير عاصم في رواية ابن عياش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers lighten the fāʾ, lengthen Zakariyyā, and place him in the nominative as the subject; two further name forms occur, with or without a final yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بتخفيف الفاء ومدوا ( زكريا ) ورفعوه على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyyā is indeclinable because it is a proper foreign name; another explanation is that it ends in the feminine alif.
rows.anchor: ومنعه من التصرف للعلمية والعجمة وقيل : لألف التأنيث

rows.speaker: أبيّ
rows.claim: Ubayy reads wa-akfalahā, ‘and He entrusted her to Zakariya.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وأكفلها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads all three verbs as prayers, with rabbahā as a vocative: ‘Accept her, Lord; nurture her; appoint Zakariya her guardian.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فتقبلها ربها وأنبتها وكفلها على صيغة الدعاء في الافعال الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Mujahid’s prayer reading, God answered Hanna’s requests in all three clauses.
rows.anchor: وقد استجاب الله تعالى دعاءها في جميع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority, supported by reports, say Zakariya cared for Maryam from the beginning; the claim that he took her only after weaning is weak.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الاكثرون وشهدت له الاخبار أن كفالة زكريا كانت من أول أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated-entry clause explains the acceptance just described and is therefore not joined with a conjunction.
rows.anchor: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب بيان لقبولها ولهذا لم يعطف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the miḥrāb as Maryam’s room in Jerusalem, with a central doorway that could be reached only by a stair, like the Kaaba’s door.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي اللهع تعالى عنهما غرفة بنيت لها في بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others understand miḥrāb as a mosque, since their mosques were called miḥrābs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد به المسجد إذ قد كانت مساجدهم تسمى المحاريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it as the mosque’s most honored front area, the imam’s place according to one opinion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أشرف مواضعه ومقدمها وهو مقام الامام من المسجد في رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb may be a place-name from the emphatic pattern mifʿāl because worshippers battle their selves there, fight Satan, or compete for it; a Maghribi poet praises courage and humility with the term.
rows.anchor: وأصله مفعال صيغة مبالغة كمطعان م فسمى به المكان لان المحاربين نفوسهم كثيرون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the adverbial phrase before the subject highlights special concern for Maryam.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الظرف على الفاعل لاظهار كمال العناية بأمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb is accusative by broadening the construction, although dakhala normally takes a preposition such as bi or ilā.
rows.anchor: ونصب ( المحراب ) على التوسع إذ حق الفعل أن يتعدى بفئ أو بالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overt subject is said to separate the clause.
rows.anchor: لفصل الجملة و ( كلما ) ظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullamā is a temporal adverb: mā is either a verbal noun with ‘time’ omitted or an indefinite relative with its antecedent deleted; the answer clause governs it by consensus.
rows.anchor: و ( كلما ) ظرف على أن ( ما ) مصدرية والزمان محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some mistakenly make the protasis itself govern kullamā as semantically more fitting; al-Alusi says this needlessly adds extra pieces to the construction.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من وهم فقال : إن ناصبه فعل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajada means Zakariya found or encountered sustenance there, or found it present in her vicinity.
rows.anchor: أى أصاب ولقى بحضرتها ذلك أو ذلك كائنا بحضرتها

rows.speaker: الزبير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from al-Zubayr that only Zakariya entered her; after he left, seven doors stood between them, yet he found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن الزبير قال : إنه كان لا يدخل عليها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite tanwīn in rizqan magnifies the sustenance.
rows.anchor: والتنوين للتعظيم فعن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sustenance consisted of fruits from Paradise.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن ذلك من أثمار الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority say it compensated Maryam for nursing, since she never nursed at a breast.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الجل أن ذلك عوض لها عن الرضاعة فقد روى أنها لم ترضع ثديا قط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Bishr via Ibn Abbas places this after Maryam was weaned at two: Zakariya hired a wet nurse, then left her alone behind a closed miḥrāb door and alone checked on her.
rows.anchor: ففي رواية ابن بشر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عايهما أن زكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام استأجر لها ظئرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He said, Maryam’ begins an explanatory resumption.
rows.anchor: قال يمريم ( استئناف بياني ( أنى لك هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks where this sustenance came from, since it was unlike worldly food and the doors were shut around her.
rows.anchor: أى من أين لك هذا الرزق الذى لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes annā to ask ‘how?’ rather than ‘from where?’; two cited lines of poetry witness the respective senses.
rows.anchor: ومجئ ( أنى ) بمعنى من أين أو كيف تقدم الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is omitted from annā, as fī is omitted with inherently locative adverbs; frequent adverbial usage permits this deletion.
rows.anchor: وحذف حرف الجر من ( أنى ) نحو حذف في من الظروف اللازمة للظرفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More generally, locatives allow deletion of their common linking preposition; omission of other prepositions is limited to indeclinable adverbs because they rank below fī.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أن الظروف محل التوسع لكثرة استعمالهم إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary provision proves that karāmāt for saints are possible, since Maryam was not a prophet according to the majority; Sunnis and Shiʿites accept this, while Muʿtazilites deny it.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز الكرامة للأولياء لأن مريم لا نبوة لها على المشهور

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi answers that the provision was an irhāṣ, a precursor to Jesus’ prophethood.
rows.anchor: وأجاب البلخي منهم عن الآية بأن ذلك كان إرهاصا وتأسيسا لنبوة عيسى

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī instead says the provision was a miracle for Zakariya.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الجبائى ي بأنه كان معجزة لزكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi objects that Zakariya’s apparent uncertainty sits poorly with al-Jubbāʾī’s miracle claim; the wording need not imply real confusion and may simply display Maryam’s wonder, while confusion about the food’s source does not rescue the claim.
rows.anchor: ورد الأخير بأن اشتباه الامر عليه يأبى ذلك ولعله مبني على الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘She said’ begins a resumption, as did the preceding ‘He said.’
rows.anchor: استئناف كالذى قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes Maryam’s answer to mean that the food came from Paradise.
rows.anchor: قيل : أرادت من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means God provided it without human mediation, so there is no reason to marvel or deem it impossible.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مما رزقنيه هو لا بواسطة البشر فلا تعجب ولا تستبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view says Maryam spoke while still a child, as Jesus did; al-Suyuti’s poem names eleven infants or children reported to have spoken.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تكلمت بذلك صغيرة كعيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وقد جمع من تكلم كذلك

rows.speaker: جلال الدين السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti’s list includes the Prophet, Yahya, Jesus, Abraham, Maryam, the witness in Joseph’s story, the child of the ditch, the infant who spoke about a nursing woman, and the child of Pharaoh’s hairdresser; it ends with a child in al-Hadi’s time.
rows.anchor: وقد نظمهم الجلال السيوطي فقال : تكلم في المهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward reading turns toward a servant marked by the station of servitude and wholly devoted to God.
rows.anchor: أو بمن اتصف بمقام العبودية وانقطع اليه بالكلية

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected lover is described through the command to follow the Prophet, the foremost of lovers, so that God will love the follower.
rows.anchor: ( قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني ) لاني سيد المحبين

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love’s reality is a heart consumed by longing, a spirit relishing love, senses immersed in intimacy, a purified soul, vision of the Beloved through all, and absorption beyond both worlds.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة المحبة عند العارفين احتراق القلب بنيران الشوق وروح الروح بلذة العشق

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love’s practical branch is conforming to all the Beloved’s wishes, receiving trials with contentment and surrender, remaining faithful, and following the Prophet’s Sunna.
rows.anchor: وأما فرعها فهو موافقة المحبوب في جميع ما يرضاه وتقبل بلائه بنعت الرضا

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its proper manners are leaving even permitted pleasures, keeping to seclusion and watchfulness, receiving intimations of divine attributes, and humility in every movement.
rows.anchor: وأما آدابها فالانقطاع عن الشهوات واللذات المباحة والسكون في الخلوات

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True love follows inner witnessing of divine beauty; love prompted by gifts is defective, since the Beloved’s essence alone should be its cause.
rows.anchor: لان المحبة متى كانت من تولد رؤية النعماء كانت معلولة

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lover does not distinguish Paradise from fire, joy from hardship, or obligation from Sunna; true love forgets all else and is absorbed in the Beloved.
rows.anchor: لا تصبح المحبة ممن يميز بين النار والجنة وبين السرور والمحنة

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry describes longing as love’s companion and compares divine love to a spark that neither flares nor dies; love must seize the whole self.
rows.anchor: يقولون إن الحب كالنار في الحشا ألا كذبوا فالنار تذكو وتخمد

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first kind is ordinary love from noticing a benefactor’s favors; it changes and belongs to workers who seek reward, as Abu al-Tayyib’s verse says.
rows.anchor: القسم الاول محبة العوام وهى مطالعة المنة من روية إحسان المحسن

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second kind is the elite’s love from reverence for God as worthy of love; it endures because beauty and majesty endure, as the report about Suhayb and Rabiʿa’s couplet illustrate.
rows.anchor: القسم الثاني ( محبة الخواص المتبعين للاخلاق الذين يحبونه إجلالا وإعظاما

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third kind arises in the elect through divine attraction and perfect gnosis; it annihilates the lover’s self, leaving the person bewildered and intoxicated, neither living nor dead.
rows.anchor: والقسم الثالث ( محبة خواص المتبعين للاحوال وهي الناشئة من الجذبة الآلهية

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sounds of ḥāʾ and bāʾ hint that love must seize heart, speech, inner and outer self before it deserves the name.
rows.anchor: ويكفي في شرح الحب لفظة فانه : حاء وباء والحاء من حروف الحلق

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s love for servants also differs by recipient: for ordinary people it appears in granting provision to whom He wills without reckoning.
rows.anchor: وأما محبة ربه سبحانه له فمختلفة أيضا وإن صدرت من محل واحد

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement has already been explained and gives the reason Maryam said the sustenance was from God.
rows.anchor: تقدم معناه والجملة تعليل لكونه من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes the closing statement Maryam’s words, included within what she said.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها من كلام مريم فحينئذ تكون في محل داخله تحت القول

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the closing words are God’s narration to the Prophet, not Maryam’s speech; al-Alusi prefers the apparent reading that she said them.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري : إنها ليست من كلامها بل هي من كلامه تعالى إخبارا لنبيه

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Abu Yaʿla transmits from Jabir that the Prophet went several days without food; Fāṭima had nothing when he visited, but a neighbor sent two loaves and meat, which she reserved for him despite her family’s hunger.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج أبو يعلي عن جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أقام أياما لم يطعم طعاما

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: The food miraculously filled Fāṭima’s bowl; she cited the same words as Maryam, and the Prophet praised her resemblance to the chief of Israel’s women, then shared the meal with his family and distributed its remainder.
rows.anchor: فلما نظرت اليها بهتت وعرفت أنها بركة من الله تعالى فحمدت الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition reflects the lack of spiritual correspondence between believers and unbelievers, like light and darkness; allegiance requires affinity, and without it becomes pretense or hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: نهى عن موالاة المؤمنين الكافرين لعدم المناسبة في الحقيقة ولفرق بين الظلمة والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of God likewise warn seekers against allegiance to deniers, whose darkness can accumulate and obstruct the path of faith.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا نهى أهل الله تعالى المريدين عن موالاة المنكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak believers may show allegiance outwardly under dissimulation, while those whose certainty is strong fear only God.
rows.anchor: ( إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ) فحينئذ تجوز الموالاة ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning calls people to direct witnessing of divine unity, so they fear no one but God; most take it as an address to gnostic elites, since only one who knows Him can fear Him.
rows.anchor: ( ويحذركم الله نفسه ) اى يدعوكم إلى التوحيد العياني لئلا يكون خوفكم

words: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: إبراهيم الخواص
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Khawwas says fear’s sign in the heart is constant watchfulness, and watchfulness is shown by checking the states that arise.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم الخواص : وعلامة الخوف في القلب دوام المراقبة

words: إِن تُخْفُوا۟ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether inner allegiance is hidden or shown, God knows it because He accompanies every breath and passing thought and knows the heavens of spirits and earth of bodies.
rows.anchor: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم ) من الموالاة ( أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ) لأنه مع كل نفس وخطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power is not distracted by one affair from another and is not confined to any manifestation.
rows.anchor: فلا يشغله شأن عن شأن ولا يقيده عن مظهر

words: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُّحْضَرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every human action and utterance leaves an imprint in the soul and is inscribed in the scrolls of celestial souls, though sensory and imaginative distractions hide it.
rows.anchor: ما يعمله الانسان أو يقوله ينتقش منه أثر في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When released from dense physical existence, a person sees these records; seeing evil, the soul wishes it were far away because the sight torments it.
rows.anchor: فاذا تجرد عن عالم الكثافة بصر ورأى وشاهد ما به قلم الاستعداد جرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated warning emphasizes that people must avoid deeds that merit divine punishment.
rows.anchor: كرره تاكيدا لئلا يعملوا ما يستحقون به عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns out of compassion for all servants, directing them to follow the Prophet and receive mercy.
rows.anchor: ( والله رءوف بالعباد ) أى بسائر فلهذا حذرهم الرحمة

words: قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ordinary people, following the Prophet with righteous deeds brings mercy; for the elite, noble character brings manifestations of divine beauty; for the elect, surrender of existence leads to divine attraction.
rows.anchor: قيل لهم : اتبعوني بالأعمال الصالحة يخصكم الله تعالى برحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the highest attraction, the distance disappears and a drop of this love suffices; even a moment of its intoxication makes time seem obedient.
rows.anchor: وهناك يرتفع البون من البين ويظهر الصبح لذي عينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness may mean pardon for prior disobedience to prophetic following, veiling the darkness of one’s traits with divine attributes, or replacing the sin of existence with abiding existence, as in the ‘I become his hearing’ report.
rows.anchor: أي معاصيكم التي سلفا منكم على خلاف المتابعة ولا يعاقبكم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God effaces sins and the darkness of attributes or existence, then grants better qualities, attributes, and true existence in their place.
rows.anchor: يكفر خطاياكم ويمحو ذنوب صفاتكم ووجودكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual disciple (murīd) must follow the one who is sought (murād).
rows.anchor: فإن المريد يلزمه متابعة المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away marks deniers who remain veiled; God does not love them because they lack capacity for the manifestation of His beauty.
rows.anchor: فهم كفار منكرون محجوبون ( والله لا يحب الكافرين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Selection is broader than love and intimate friendship and includes all prophets, though their degrees differ, as the verse on messengers’ differing ranks indicates.
rows.anchor: الاصطفاء أعم من المحبة والخلة فيشمل الأنبياء كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love is the most particular rank, friendship comes next, and selection is broadest; the wording of khulla hints at this through its articulation.
rows.anchor: فأخص المراتب هو المحبة وإليه يشير قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s selection signifies teaching him the attributes and the two hands, with all created beings commanded to prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: فاصطفى آدم بتعليم الصفات وجمع اليدين وإسجاد الأكوان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is the second father, selected through that paternity and through his dealings with his people.
rows.anchor: ونوحا الذي هو الأب الثاني بتلك الأبوة وبما كان له مع قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family of Abraham means the prophets descended from him, whose existence received the lights of a special divine manifestation.
rows.anchor: واصطفى آل إبراهيم وهم الأنبياء من ذريته بظهور انوار تجليه الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The families are one another’s descendants spiritually as well as physically: every prophet’s follower in unity, gnosis, and inward fundamentals is his child, like a shaykh’s disciple.
rows.anchor: ذرية بعضها من بعض في الدين والحقيقة إذ الولادة قسمان

words: آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another symbolic scheme makes Adam the spirit’s first descent, Noah its second, Abraham the heart cast by the nafs into trials, Abraham’s family the spiritual powers, and Imran the intellect in the body’s sanctuary with its followers.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : آدم هو الروح في أول مقامات ظهورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This symbolic lineage reflects a common source and shared spiritual path.
rows.anchor: وكل ذلك ذرية بعضها لوحدة المورد واتفاق المشرب

words: نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanna’s vow inwardly frees the child from the lower soul’s bondage, making the child sincere in worship and unattached to anything besides God.
rows.anchor: عن رق النفس مخلصا في عبادتك عن الميل إلى السوى

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti interprets Maryam’s good acceptance as her being protected from creatures’ perception.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : محفوظ عن إدراك الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her good growth is being watered by the waters of divine power and made fruitful as a tree of prophethood.
rows.anchor: حيث سقاها من مياه القدرة وأثمرها شجرة النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya’s guardianship reflects the purity of his inward secret and the attraction of like to like.
rows.anchor: لطهارة سره وشبيه السئ منجذب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward sustenance is spiritual knowledge, realities, sciences, and wisdoms flowing from God; the phrase ‘with Him’ marks it as nobler than bodily food.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد الرزق الروحاني من المعارف والحقائق والعلوم والحكم
